note: Live controls for internal/tui, the two-pane navigator. Golden frames are regression cover, not controls: a frame test fails on any byte diff and therefore proves nothing about a specific clause, which is this repository's dominant defect class wearing a costume. These sit on the load-bearing branches qy3de.11, qy3de.6 and qy3de.7 name — the cursor's id-tracking, the filter predicate, the truncation rule, the row set's status filter, the picker's row/line coordinate conversion, the direction of every relation heading, the modal's row-applicability logic, the editor's two refusals, the reopen prompt and the warning sink — split by branch where one clause is too coarse to mutate in one place. Seeded by qy3de.11; the follow half added by qy3de.12; the write set by qy3de.13.

controls.clause: The cursor tracks an issue ID and not a row index, so a reload that reorders rows cannot move the selection under the reader (qy3de.4, named there as a control rather than a preference)
When the tracked id leaves the row set — filtered out, closed with `C` off, deleted — the cursor holds the position index that row last occupied, clamped, rather than jumping to the top (qy3de.4)
`/` matches case-insensitively, so a lowercase needle finds a capitalised title (qy3de.4)
`/` is a substring over the id AND the title, because ids are structured and looking one up is half of what the filter is for (qy3de.4)

The ` [N]` marker is appended AFTER the title is cut, so the cut pays for it and a blocked row is never wider than its pane (euv2e.4 recorded this trap; qy3de.5 measured a 13-column marker leaving negative room on all 13 blocked rows)
The id column auto-sizes to the widest id present but never past twelve columns, because pad-to-widest spends twenty dead columns on 44 rows to fit two (qy3de.4)

An id past the cap is truncated through render's own ellipsis rule rather than overflowing its column — the pane deliberately breaks render's never-truncate-an-identifier rule, and the mark is what makes that honest (qy3de.3, qy3de.4)
The project column, shown only under `a`, is capped at twelve the same way: eight of the ten projects holding open issues have slugs of nine columns or fewer and cover 172 of 174 rows (qy3de.4)
The row set is `list`'s contract — open AND in_progress — not `ready`'s, because Ready and Blocked cannot see an in_progress issue and so would structurally hide the one you are working on (qy3de.4)
`C` includes closed issues in the row set, which is a 6.3x row jump in `drops` and is why it is disclosed in the footer as a word rather than a glyph (qy3de.4)
The detail pane renders through render.Console into a buffer at the MEASURED pane width, so a resize re-wraps the page rather than clipping one wrapped for the old width (qy3de.3)
controls.old: console := render.Console{Out: &buf, Width: width, TTY: false}
controls.new: console := render.Console{Out: &buf, Width: render.DefaultWidth, TTY: false}

controls.clause: lipgloss Style.Width is the TOTAL rendered width, borders included, so a pane of N content columns asks for N+2 — getting it backwards leaves the top edge and the body two columns apart (qy3de.2, qy3de.5)

Heights are managed by pad and never by a Style, because lipgloss Height() is the OUTER height and leaving it to a Style left the two panes at different heights (euv2e.4's trap, paid for in one place by qy3de.5)
The footer names the visible column window and the widest line whenever the page overflows the pane and is not wrapped, so a clipped table row does not read as a whole row (qy3de.5)
picker.move clamps the cursor to [0, len(rows)-1] at both ends, which is also what makes `g` and `G` a delta longer than the list rather than two more branches (qy3de.6 §10 control 1)

view emits a group header exactly where the group CHANGES — not once per row (qy3de.6 §10 control 2). Headers are never stored as rows, which is what removes the skip-the-header branch rather than testing it

The same clause's other wrong implementation: a header emitted only above the FIRST row leaves every later group unlabelled, which is what a picker over seven relation kinds cannot survive (qy3de.6 §5, §10 control 2)
scroll windows on the cursor's RENDERED LINE, not its row index — the one place the two coordinates disagree, because every header above a row shifts it down (qy3de.6 §10 control 3)

view re-derives the same window from the cursor's rendered line, so a picker drawn without a scroll — after a resize, or in a test — still shows the row under the cursor (qy3de.6 §10 control 3, the second place the conversion happens)

A `blocks` OUT edge is what blocks this issue and an IN edge is what this issue blocks: the direction is named from the reader's end, the opposite of the edge's own (qy3de.6 §10 control 4). A swapped pair survives a round trip and reads plausibly, which is why each kind is its own control

`A discovered-from B` means A was derived from B, so the OUT edge is where this issue came from — `Discovered from` — and the IN edge is what came out of it — `Discovered` (qy3de.6 §5, §10 control 4). This is the pair no other surface in drops renders at all (drops://hxedy), so nothing else would catch a swap
`related` is undirected, so it is ONE group holding both directions rather than a pair of headings named from an end that does not exist (qy3de.6 §5)

The picker's id column auto-sizes to the widest id IN THAT PICKER and does NOT inherit the left pane's twelve-column cap: a picker's rows are by construction siblings, and seven of gitops-vn4's sixteen live children collapse to the same twelve columns (qy3de.6 §4, §10 control 5)
`f` on an issue with no relations opens nothing and says `nothing to follow`, rather than an empty modal that captures every key with nothing to choose (qy3de.6 §2, §10 control 6)
`backspace` at depth 0 is a no-op, not a pop off an empty stack (qy3de.6 §10 control 7)

Moving the left cursor clears the follow stack. This is the control under a key REMOVED from the design: euv2e.5's `esc clears the stack` was dropped because `j` — a key you were about to press — already does it (qy3de.6 §7, §10 control 8)
`x` on a tombstoned issue opens no modal at all and says so, because every core write refuses one with ErrConflict and a modal of six verbs that all fail is worse than none (qy3de.7 §8)
The modal offers `close` on live work and `reopen` on a closed issue, never both and never the wrong one (qy3de.7 §8)

`claim` and `release` are withheld from a closed issue even though ClaimIssue permits one: 38 of the live store's 39 assignees sit on closed issues, so the claim is the durable record of who resolved a ticket (qy3de.7 §8)
`release` appears only on a claimed issue and `claim` only on an unclaimed one, so neither verb is ever offered where core would refuse it (qy3de.7 §8)

`x` acts on whatever the RIGHT PANE is showing — the followed target when the stack is non-empty, the cursor's issue otherwise. euv2e.6 said "the right pane's issue" before there was a follow stack that could make the two differ (qy3de.7 §8)
An empty or whitespace-only editor file writes no close at all — a real divergence from the CLI, where `--reason` is optional and `drops close <id>` legally stores NULL (qy3de.7 §3)
An empty or whitespace-only editor file writes no comment AND says nothing: letting core refuse it as ErrInvalid would put an error on the message line for something that did not happen (qy3de.7 §3)
A non-zero editor exit discards the file however full it is, which is what makes `:cq` a deliberate cancel rather than a silent loss (qy3de.7 §3)

`reopen`'s prompt reports the ACTUAL length of the close_reason SetIssueStatus is about to null out. It is not an "are you sure": it states the size of what is lost, which is the one thing the reader cannot otherwise see (qy3de.7 §7)
Every key but `y` answers the reopen prompt with no, so a keypress that was not an answer cannot destroy a close reason (qy3de.7 §7)
A credential pattern in a comment body produces a VISIBLE line rather than a silent stderr write, which under an alt screen is the same as no warning at all (qy3de.7 §5)

A write refused by core — realistically a claim landing between the render and the `enter` — leaves the store as it was and says so on the message line, which is the only place it can be seen under a full-screen program (qy3de.7 §10)

The re-read after a write RESTORES the cursor onto its tracked id rather than holding an index, so a priority change — which re-orders the list, since `ORDER BY issues.priority` is the store's first key — carries the cursor to the row's new position instead of selecting someone else (qy3de.7 §9)
The message line is taken out of the PANES, so qy3de.4's disclosure line and qy3de.5's scroll indicator are undisturbed while it is up, and the row comes back when it clears (qy3de.7 §10)
